newsitem.title: ANGOLA: IMF chief arrives in Angola to assess economy.
newsitem.headline: IMF chief arrives in Angola to assess economy.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director Michel Camdessus arrived in Angola on Monday for a three-day visit to assess the country's economy.

The IMF withdrew its representative from Angola last year due to the government's failure to implement economic reforms and said it would return only if there were concrete efforts to bring about economic change.
Finance Minister Alcantara Monteiro met Camdessus at Luanda airport.

"We hope the IMF, which knows perfectly well the real situation in the country and has shown a certain flexibility in the application of its programme, will realise that we are a special case," Monteiro told reporters.
Camdessus did not speak to reporters on arrival.

Angola is keen to obtain IMF help in rebuilding its economy, battered by a war of independence against Portugal and then 19 years of civil war. The fighting was ended by a peace pact signed in November 1994.
